channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Dino marca para 16 de junho o julgamento Eduardo Bolsonaro por coação
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino has scheduled Eduardo Bolsonaro's trial for coercion in the course of proceedings for June 16. The Prosecutor General's Office argues he used political influence to impose sanctions on Brazilian officials and shield his father, Jair Bolsonaro, from accountability for the January 8 attacks. The trial will be heard by Dino, Alexandre de Moraes, Cristiano Zanin, and Cármen Lúcia, with Eduardo Bolsonaro defended by the Public Defender's Union.

item.title: As emissoras de TV que saltaram em faturamento no governo Lula
item.description: Under Lula's government, TV broadcasters' revenue from federal advertising increased by 46% compared to the Bolsonaro administration, reaching nearly R$ 500 million. Globo almost tripled its earnings, while Record saw a 20% increase, and SBT and Jovem Pan lost ground, with reductions of 19% and 41%, respectively. TV Cultura was the biggest winner, with its revenue quadrupling.

item.title: Reunião ministerial tem alerta sobre restrições nas eleições e pedido por verde-amarelo na Copa
item.description: During a ministerial meeting at the Planalto Palace, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva reiterated his request for ministers to wear green and yellow clothing during World Cup matches, as part of a broader strategy to reclaim national symbols previously associated with Bolsonarism. Minister of Social Communication Sidônio Palmeira also warned colleagues to carefully observe electoral blackout rules in compliance with legislation ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Governo vê tarifa dos EUA por trabalho forçado como pressão comercial
item.description: The Brazilian government dismisses as 'absurd' the U.S. proposal to impose an additional 12.5% tariff on Brazilian imports over alleged failures to combat forced labor, asserting Brazil is a global reference in this area per the ILO. If applied, the tariff could reach up to 37% when combined with existing 25% duties, prompting Brazil to threaten reciprocity under its Reciprocity Law, with negotiations underway to avoid implementation by July 15. Ethanol is cited as the only product clearly featured in tariff talks, while critical minerals and big tech remain outside Brazil’s agenda.

item.title: Dino marca julgamento de Eduardo Bolsonaro, réu por coação
item.description: Minister Flávio Dino, president of the First Chamber of the STF, scheduled Eduardo Bolsonaro’s trial for June 16 on charges of coercion. He is accused of pressuring Brazilian authorities from the United States to interfere in the coup attempt case, with the PGR seeking conviction for acts of hostility and international retaliation promises. The trial follows a request by Minister Alexandre de Moraes, the case rapporteur, and occurs amid efforts to include Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the investigation.

item.title: Lula cobra que ministros divulguem ações de outras pastas e não só das próprias
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva instructed his ministers to promote initiatives from all government departments, not just their own portfolios, during a ministerial meeting at the Planalto Palace on Wednesday (June 3). The goal is to create a unified and integrated narrative, ensuring 'everyone is on the same page,' especially since recent programs like Desenrola, Move Aplicativos, and the end of taxation on small clothing items have not received expected visibility. The move also aims to strengthen communication ahead of the electoral calendar, with this meeting possibly being one of the last with the full first tier before the recess.

item.title: O novo tarifaço e a falta de um projeto de país
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are engaged in a public dispute over responsibility for a potential U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, currently under review by the Trump administration. Lula accuses Flávio of lacking White House communication, while Bolsonaro’s son criticizes the federal government’s foreign policy. The clash highlights the absence of a coherent national project amid external pressures.

item.title: Troca de farpas entre Lula e Flávio adia debate importante, dizem economistas
item.description: Economists warn that escalating trade tensions between Brazil and the United States, with new U.S. tariff threats, are increasing uncertainty for Brazilian exporters, prompting revisions in investment and production strategies. High-value-added sectors such as manufacturing, machinery, and aerospace are most vulnerable, while agribusiness has some mitigation mechanisms. Markets are in a holding pattern, awaiting concrete signals of a reversal, underscoring the importance of Brazilian diplomacy and corporate engagement with U.S. authorities.

item.title: A ‘lição’ que Lula está aprendendo em meio à nova surpresa de Donald Trump
item.description: New U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods — including Pix, ethanol, and deforestation-linked products — have heightened diplomatic tensions between Lula and Trump, frustrating the Brazilian president who expected more predictable negotiations after recent talks. The exclusion of Brazil from the U.S. list of Latin American allies by Marco Rubio, combined with expert analysis from Uriã Fancelli, suggests the tariffs are driven by political and ideological motives, serving as domestic electoral tools for Trumpism, despite most costs being absorbed by U.S. businesses and consumers.

item.title: Indicação de embaixador de Trump e Marco Rubio acendem alerta no governo Lula
item.description: The appointment of Republican ambassador Daniel Perez to Brazil, combined with statements by Secretary of State Marco Rubio referencing the Brazilian electoral process, has raised alarms in the Lula government over perceived ideological alignment with Trumpism and Bolsonarist right-wing factions, suggesting potential U.S. influence in the 2026 presidential election. Analysts argue the move reflects Washington’s strategic interest in Brazil and interpret Rubio’s comments as an overt signal favoring a political shift toward a more U.S.-allied government in Brasília.

item.title: Reguladoras planejam cortar serviços após bloqueio milionário no orçamento
item.description: The blocking of R$23.7 billion in the federal budget, signed by President Lula on May 30, 2026, cut 18% of funds for Brazil’s 12 federal regulatory agencies, prompting some to plan service and oversight reductions. The ANTT suffered the largest cut at R$57 million, threatening federal auctions, public hearings, and road freight floor enforcement, while Aneel, ANP, and Anvisa face delays in office expansions, fuel quality controls, and sanitary monitoring. Experts warn that weakened regulation could fuel fraud, organized crime infiltration, and harm both consumers and compliant companies.

item.title: Lula pede para ministros não apresentarem “nada novo” até o fim das eleições
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) urged government ministers to refrain from presenting new projects until the end of the 2024 municipal elections, focusing instead on delivering already-planned initiatives. The request was made during a ministerial meeting at the Palácio do Planalto, with Lula stating there is time until July 3 to complete what has already been conceived.

item.title: Marco Rubio é “um latino-americano frustrado”, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula criticized U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, calling him a 'frustrated Latin American' during a ministerial meeting at the Planalto Palace. Lula said Rubio treats Latin America and Brazil poorly, and noted he had previously expressed this view to President Trump.

item.title: “Não podemos aceitar o tratamento que os EUA deram ao Brasil”, diz Lula
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the proposal by the U.S. Office of the Trade Representative to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian imports, stating that Brazil cannot accept such treatment. He emphasized that the country is in a moment of defending its economic sovereignty and stressed the need for a firm response to U.S. protectionist measures.

item.title: Lula avalia plano ‘dois em um’ após novo tarifaço de Trump
item.description: The Lula government is evaluating a 'two-in-one' plan to counter the new U.S. tariffs: publicly hardening its stance against Trump while pursuing private negotiations to mitigate economic damage. The trade crisis, triggered by U.S. tariffs of 10% to 12.5% on Brazilian goods over forced labor allegations, is seen as a political opportunity to highlight the Bolsonaro family's perceived subservience to Washington.

item.title: Lula pede que ministros organizem entregas até 3 de julho
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged ministers to accelerate program execution and organize government deliveries by July 3, ahead of electoral restrictions. He emphasized completing already-announced projects, avoiding new initiatives, and improving coordination with the Civil House to prevent unannounced inaugurations. Lula also criticized unilateral actions by ministers, called for internal alignment amid political and ideological tensions, and directed the government to seek alternative markets if U.S. trade relations deteriorate.

item.title: Belchior apresenta balanço do governo em reunião ministerial
item.description: Minister Miriam Belchior presented the federal government's progress report in a ministerial meeting with President Lula, highlighting that Brazil achieved for the first time a very high human development index (IDH). She also reported advances in the Desenrola Brasil program (1.4 million debt renegotiations for families, 85,000 for companies and 28,000 for rural sectors), along with results in public security (over 6,000 arrests in Operation Woman Safe and nearly 500 in integrated actions against organized crime), and initiatives in health, housing and the environment.

item.title: Plateia do Fórum de Lisboa aplaude quando Gonet elogia Moraes
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet praised Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for his role in the January 8 case during the 14th Lisbon Forum, emphasizing his courage and firmness. The audience applauded when Gonet mentioned Moraes, who was present. Both advocated for international regulation of big techs to safeguard national sovereignty and democracy.

item.title: Fachin fala em “discrição” e critica o “protagonismo individual” de juízes
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin advocated for judicial 'institutional silence' over individual prominence to preserve the Judiciary's image and legitimacy in a polarized society. He stressed that public trust depends on judicial integrity, discretion, and decision quality, not on frequent public statements. Fachin also emphasized that judicial ethics must be indivisible between public and private life.

item.title: “Vai que Deus resolve”, diz Flávio sobre vitória em 1º turno
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) argued that a right-wing victory in the first round of the 2026 elections is possible and desirable, stating "maybe God will settle it in the first round". He called for unity among conservative leaders, naming Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), to build an alternative to President Lula and the PT, warning that another PT term would lead Brazil into economic and social decline.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz esperar união com Zema e Caiado no 2º turno para ‘derrotar o PT’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) said he is seeking unity with Romeu Zema (Novo) and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) to defeat the PT in a potential 2026 election runoff, describing their talks as frank and direct. He criticized Zema for prematurely releasing a video attacking his conversations with banker Daniel Vorcaro, but stressed the need for the three to unite against Lula. Flávio also stated he would appoint a conservative to the STF if elected and expressed difficulty forming a Minas Gerais gubernatorial ticket with current governor Mateus Simões (PSD) due to opposing party alignments.

item.title: Brasil vai buscar novos parceiros para diminuir impactos comerciais
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil will seek new trade partners to counter the impact of proposed U.S. trade policies, including a potential 25% tariff on Brazilian exports. He affirmed national sovereignty, rejected submissive posturing toward global powers, and announced his unexpected attendance at the G7 summit in June in France as a guest of President Emmanuel Macron, aiming to advocate for multilateralism reform and UN strengthening.

item.title: Toffoli reconsidera e dá vitória parcial a Vaccari na Lava Jato
item.description: Supreme Federal Court Justice Dias Toffoli reversed his prior ruling and partially granted a petition by João Vaccari Neto, former PT treasurer, ordering Brasília’s 1st Electoral Zone to reassess evidence in a Lava Jato-related case. The move follows claims that Vaccari’s case was not properly archived despite Toffoli’s 2025 annulment of proceedings against him.

item.title: Flávio diz esperar que Trump atenda ao seu pedido para não haver mais tarifação sobre produtos brasileiros
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro says he expects President Donald Trump to heed his request to avoid a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods proposed by the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), citing Brazilian policies on PIX, deforestation, and digital regulations as justification. He blames the Lula administration’s allegedly hostile stance toward the U.S. and its rapprochement with China for the trade tension, advocating for a more balanced foreign policy that serves Brazilian interests.

item.title: Kassio é sorteado para relatar processo de Michelle contra Janones por post sobre ‘dinheiro roubado’
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Kassio Nunes Marques has been appointed as rapporteur in a criminal complaint filed by former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro against federal deputy André Janones for libel, defamation, and insult, over a social media post claiming she would benefit from money allegedly stolen by the Bolsonaro family in a deal with Banco Master. Michelle seeks conviction and at least BRL 20,000 in moral damages. Justice Marques has not yet issued a ruling in the case.

item.title: Lula sobe o tom contra os EUA, chama Rubio de ‘frustrado’ e anuncia ida ao G7
item.description: President Lula increased his criticism of the United States, calling new tariff threats inadequate and surprising, especially following his May meeting with Trump. He labeled Secretary of State Marco Rubio a 'frustrated Latin American' and announced he would send a new letter to Trump, emphasizing his intent to maintain dialogue despite rising tensions.

item.title: ‘Não podemos aceitar o tratamento que os Estados Unidos deram ao Brasil nesta semana’, diz Lula
item.description: President Lula criticized the U.S. proposal to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, stating Brazil will not accept the treatment received this week. He said he will send another letter to Trump and write articles in American and global press to show the U.S. is wrong and causing unnecessary violence. Lula also noted the U.S. has had a trade surplus with Brazil for the last 15 years and accused Secretary of State Marco Rubio of disliking Latin America.

item.title: Lula diz que foi pego de 'surpresa' com tarifas propostas e que vai enviar nova carta a Trump
item.description: Lula stated he was not officially notified by U.S. authorities about new trade tariffs on Brazilian products, calling the move a surprising and unacceptable action. He recalled a three-hour meeting with Trump where he proposed a 30-day deadline for trade ministers to reach an agreement, which has not yet been concluded. While reaffirming Brazil's interest in strengthening ties with the U.S., Lula criticized the treatment received and referred to Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a 'frustrated Latin American'.

item.title: Lula afirma que tratamento dado pelos EUA é inaceitável e diz que pessoas tentam trair o Brasil com 'interesses rasteiros' e eleitorais
item.description: President Lula criticized the treatment of Brazil by the United States, calling new proposed tariffs unacceptable and accusing some Brazilians of attempting to harm the country for petty electoral interests. He claimed these actors were betraying the nation by seeking political gain through foreign sanctions, emphasizing that the real victims are the Brazilian people. Lula also stated that Brazil must not be treated as an 'insignificant banana republic'.

item.title: Em reunião ministerial, Lula cobra equipe sobre entregas antes das eleições e exibe frase: 'O PIX é do Brasil'
item.description: During a ministerial meeting, President Lula urged his team to deliver results before the 2026 elections and displayed the slogan 'PIX is Brazil's' in response to new U.S. tariffs. He argued the tariffs are based on false claims, noting the U.S. trade deficit with Brazil is actually in Brazil's favor, and accused unnamed actors of betraying the nation for petty electoral interests, implicitly referencing Bolsonaro's allies.

item.title: TSE e Defensorias assinam acordo de assistência jurídica a candidatos e eleitores vulneráveis
item.description: The TSE, Anadep, and Condege signed a technical cooperation agreement to provide free legal assistance to candidates and voters in economic vulnerability, effective Monday (8). The initiative aims to ensure access to electoral justice and strengthen democracy, particularly in contexts of social inequality.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Novo tarifaço de Trump pauta presidenciáveis e reforça percepção no Planalto de tentativa de interferência eleitoral
item.description: The threat of a new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian products has become a central theme in the 2026 presidential pre-campaign, with Lula using it to reinforce a narrative of national sovereignty, particularly tying it to the popularity of Pix as an economic independence symbol. Flávio Bolsonaro countered by blaming Lula’s aggressive rhetoric toward the U.S. for the tariff attempt. Government officials view Trump’s move as an effort to interfere in Brazil’s election, even if driven also by commercial interests in critical minerals and big tech regulation.

item.title: Estratégia do governo Lula é dizer que Flávio Bolsonaro quer tirar PIX do BC e entregar para setor privado
item.description: The Lula government is employing a strategy of accusing Flávio Bolsonaro of seeking to transfer control of Brazil’s PIX payment system from the Central Bank to the private sector, particularly American credit card networks, to undermine his candidacy. The government also claims Bolsonaro would promise to hand over critical mineral exploration to the Trump administration and liberalize digital platforms in Brazil, allegations his team denies, stating he only seeks cooperation with the U.S., not submission.

item.title: Flávio diz que tarifa é do Lula, e Pix é 'do Brasil e de Bolsonaro'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) claimed that the new tariffs proposed by the United States are the responsibility of President Lula (PT), calling them 'Lula's tariff'. He also stated that Pix is 'Brazil's and Bolsonaro's', in response to Lula calling him a traitor and an imbecile.

item.title: Ex-deputado George Santos é investigado por fraude em apostas nos EUA
item.description: Former U.S. congressman George Santos, of Brazilian descent, is under investigation by the U.S. Department of Justice for suspected fraud in prediction markets on the platform Kalshi, after betting against his own attendance at President Donald Trump’s State of the Union address despite publicly stating he would attend. Kalshi flagged suspicious trading activity before the event, when Santos’ attendance odds were near 75%, and he later claimed to have been detained at the airport minutes after the speech began. Santos was previously convicted in 2024 of fraud and identity theft, serving only 84 days before receiving a presidential pardon from Trump.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula promove reunião ministerial
item.description: President Lula chaired the second ministerial meeting of the year on June 3, 2026, to coordinate the government's response to escalating trade and security tensions with the United States. The meeting followed new U.S. tariff threats, including a proposed 25% duty on Brazilian goods over unfair trade practices and a 12.5% rate linked to forced labor, alongside the designation of PCC and CV as foreign terrorist organizations. The gathering aimed to align ministerial messaging amid the most strained bilateral relations in recent years.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 3 de junho
item.description: JCaesar's June 3, 2026 cartoon satirizes the relationship between Donald Trump and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, using commercial tariffs as the backdrop for political humor. The image likely critiques trade tensions between the U.S. and Brazil, portraying Trump as aggressive in his tariff policies and Lula as a figure attempting to navigate or respond to these pressures.

item.title: Lula faz reunião ministerial para alinhar governo antes da campanha e discutir tensão com os EUA
item.description: President Lula convenes his ministers at the Planalto Palace to align the government ahead of the 2026 elections and amid escalating trade tensions with the United States, following a U.S. recommendation for 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods. The meeting aims to unify messaging on government achievements and the response to U.S. measures, which the Planalto attributes to the Bolsonaro family's actions.

item.title: Tarifas dos EUA colocam comércio exterior e eleições na mesma arena
item.description: The USTR proposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, with exceptions for strategic sectors like beef, linking trade policy to the 2026 electoral landscape. The measure intensifies pressure on candidates to debate foreign policy and its economic impact on Brazil.

item.title: Análise: conta de tarifaço 2.0 está na mesa do bolsonarismo
item.description: The new 25% U.S. tariff on Brazil, dubbed 'tariff hike 2.0', has entered the 2026 pre-campaign as a central issue, with Lula and right-wing pre-candidates debating who will bear the cost. The measure is seen as a repeat of earlier episodes tied to Bolsonarist allies’ lobbying in the U.S., particularly Flávio Bolsonaro’s trip aiming to gain political capital by designating criminal factions as terrorist groups, which instead linked him to the tariff. Despite attempts to distance, political responsibility falls on the Bolsonarist camp.

item.title: O petista que cunhou o apelido 'Tariflávio'
item.description: The PT launched the nickname 'Tariflávio' for Flávio Bolsonaro, linking him to a proposed 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods. The initiative was shared on the party’s social media platforms yesterday morning as part of a political communication strategy. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Governo Lula já esperava novas sanções dos EUA por trabalho forçado e vai insistir no discurso eleitoral de soberania nacional
item.description: The Lula government anticipated new U.S. sanctions over alleged forced labor and will maintain a national sovereignty discourse in its official responses. The proposed tariffs are 12.5% on Brazilian products, part of a Section 301 investigation that also targets 59 other countries. The U.S. strategy aims to rebuild trade barriers on a stronger legal footing after a Supreme Court defeat.

item.title: De aborto à maioridade penal, oposição no Congresso tenta aprovar propostas que são bandeiras eleitorais antes da campanha
item.description: Opposition lawmakers are advancing right-wing electoral proposals ahead of the 2026 elections, including lowering the age of criminal responsibility to 14, loosening gun ownership requirements, and restricting legal abortion for minors under 14. These initiatives are tied to the pre-campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), who has endorsed reducing the age of criminal responsibility as a response to juvenile crime. The bill restricting abortion for children has already been approved by the Senate and will take effect, while other measures remain under congressional review.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro abusam da retórica e fazem comédia de erros
item.description: Lula accused Flávio Bolsonaro and his family of being 'traitors of the homeland' for allegedly seeking foreign intervention in Brazilian affairs, comparing them to historical traitor Joaquim Silvério dos Reis. Flávio Bolsonaro countered by claiming Lula was encouraging criminal factions to kill him and threatened to take the matter to the STF, alleging the president wanted him hanged like Tiradentes. The exchange of harsh rhetoric raised concerns that the campaign is devolving into a 'comedy of errors'.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1 sai antes da eleição? As pressões a favor e contra na reta final no Congresso
item.description: The proposal to end the 6x1 work scale was approved in the Chamber of Deputies, but its progress in the Senate remains uncertain due to President Davi Alcolumbre's cautious stance, advocating for calm debate and committee analysis before plenary vote. Meanwhile, 41 opposition senators, including pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, introduced an alternative PEC preserving the current work schedule and offering a flexible hours-based regime, without reducing weekly hours or guaranteeing two days off per week.

item.title: Viana, Cameli e Bittar empatam por vagas ao Senado no AC
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey released on June 3, 2026 shows a technical tie between Jorge Viana (PT), Gladson Cameli (PP) and Márcio Bittar (PL) in the race for Senate seats in Acre, with a 3.2-point margin of error. The study, registered with the TSE under AC-01182/2026, interviewed 1,000 people from May 31 to June 2, 2026, at a cost of R$40,000 funded by own resources. Since each state elects two senators in 2026, the total percentages do not sum to 100%.

item.title: Tiro ao Pix pode ser fatal para Flávio
item.description: The United States' threat to limit or embargo the use of Pix through tariffs or sanctions could significantly influence Brazil's 2026 elections, particularly if framed as an attack on national sovereignty. For Flávio Bolsonaro, running for Senate or another office, this issue could become a critical vulnerability, given his base's sensitivity to technological autonomy and resistance to foreign interference. The article suggests that if effectively amplified by opponents, such measures could undermine his credibility and popular support.

item.title: O novo tarifaço dará mais combustível às narrativas das campanhas de Lula e Flávio
item.description: The campaigns of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro immediately used Donald Trump's new tariff announcement as an opportunity to reinforce their electoral narratives. Lula sought to link the measure to the risks of protectionism and international dependence, while Flávio Bolsonaro employed it to criticize global policies and defend national sovereignty, adapting their speeches throughout the day. The strategy reflects how external events are rapidly absorbed into Brazil's political disputes.

item.title: Possível novo tarifaço dos EUA reforça necessidade de MP do Brasil Soberano 2, que pode ter ajustes para enquadrar atingidos, diz Mercadante
item.description: BNDES President Aloizio Mercadante says new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods reinforce the urgency of approving the Brazil Soberano 2 provisional measure (MP 1345), which may be adjusted to include affected sectors. He dismisses U.S. claims of 'unfair competition' by Pix and 'forced labor' as absurd, emphasizing that Pix is a spontaneous, efficient technological innovation already replacing traditional payment methods and poised to transform foreign trade. Mercadante adds that resistance comes mainly from big techs, which aim to control financial operations via AI and view Pix as a competitive threat due to its zero cost and widespread adoption.

item.title: MP vai ampliar uso de provas criminais em todo o país para barrar candidatos de facções mesmo antes de condenação
item.description: The Electoral Public Prosecutor's Office will direct prosecutors to use evidence of politicians' ties to criminal gangs, gathered in criminal investigations, to challenge candidacies even without a judicial conviction. The goal is to block candidates linked to organized crime from running in elections, based on 2024 jurisprudence and constitutional interpretation prohibiting parties from using paramilitary organizations. The Task Force on Combating Organized Crime in the Electoral Sphere will release a technical note with past cases of criminal infiltration into public office to guide 2026 electoral actions.
